Thermal model predicts no limit breach in 60-120min (peak margin -5.7C). No auto mitigation justified; recommend prompt human inspection of Rack B feed connector.

data.text:
No thermal hazard developing yet — no action taken.

- Trigger: Rack B voltage drop 181 mV (+92 mV), jumping from ~95 to 181 mV in last 8 min, while total power steady at ~4.6 kW.
- All sensors trusted, none flat/stuck.
- Diagnose: posterior 1.0 for loose connector on Rack B feed (~0.10 ohm, onset ~5 min ago), p_fault=1.
- Hidden-zone estimate: rack B 28.4C, connector 30.9C, well within limits.
- Tested 3 actions in simulation over 60-120 min: dispatch human check, power-cap rack B 70%, cut power circuit B. All show p_breach=0 with and without action, peak margin -5.7C. So no automatic mitigation is demonstrably better than doing nothing, and drastic cut would not help thermally.

Electrical contact is degrading and should be inspected promptly for fire/electrical risk, notified as info. Recommend human check of Rack B feed connector soon, but no emergency power cut or cooling action justified by simulated thermal limits.
